query:
The Clay & Fire Collective operates on an apparent norm that work in progress is not photographed or shared without the maker's permission. Does this norm apply equally to all members?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Reuben
C. Simone
D. Yuki
context:
[1] (about=Simone, episodic, t6 @2026-04-12T10:37:00) I can take the photos for everyone if people want?? I've gotten pretty good at ceramics photography
[2] (about=Callum, episodic, t8 @2026-05-17T10:11:00) Yes, please do. That was actually on my list -- I wanted someone to photograph the full set laid out before I pack them. Make sure you get the rim detail in natural light if you can. The translucency only shows properly in daylight.
[3] (about=Nadia, episodic, t6 @2026-04-12T10:23:00) okay switching gears -- I've been in touch with the studio about exhibiting some work at their open day in June. they do a small member showcase and they've asked if any of us want to put pieces in. I'm submitting three pieces from the gas reduction session, the matte grey ones. who else is interested? this is genuinely low stakes, no jury, no sales, just a display. 🎨
[4] (about=Nadia, episodic, t9 @2026-06-14T09:52:00) okay so here's the thing -- the studio open day is in two weeks and I want to finalise who is putting work in. I have three pieces confirmed from me. Reuben, you mentioned the large square vessel. Simone, I assume the teal bowl. Yuki -- still a maybe? I need to know by Wednesday so I can submit the combined list. 📋
[5] (about=Nadia, episodic, t10 @2026-06-14T10:01:00) they allow two pieces per maker so yes, both can go in. Reuben: title, material, and approximate dimensions on the cards, that's all. I'll print them, just send me the details by Friday. 🖨️
[6] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-08-23T10:04:00) fair enough, Reuben -- I'll circulate the date and we can see how many finished pieces the group has by then. if the work isn't ready the session can stay as working time. what I won't do is cancel the booking because we might not have enough pieces. 😄
[7] (about=Reuben, episodic, t14 @2026-08-23T09:57:00) September works. October I'd rather keep the making time intact. A full critique session only makes sense if people are bringing work that's ready. I've never found the conversation useful unless the pieces are genuinely done.
[8] (about=Reuben, episodic, t14 @2026-08-23T10:16:00) Technically speaking, that approach works until you're trying to develop as a maker rather than produce pieces you like. There's no law against it but it does create a ceiling.
[9] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-08-23T10:12:00) I think that's right for your work, Reuben. I come at it differently -- I sometimes need to make the surface to understand the form. but that's because I throw, and the relationship between clay and tool is more immediate for me. hand-building is more deliberate from the start. 🏺
[10] (about=Reuben, episodic, t10 @2026-06-14T10:08:00) Four works fine. I would want any new member to be a serious maker, not someone in the beginner workshop stage.
agent_answer: There is no information available in the conversation to answer this question.
